rules.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR THORACIC SPINE CT / Evaluation of Neurologic Deficits (1) / When Thoracic Spine MRI is Contraindicated or cannot be performed
rules.source_quote: When Thoracic Spine MRI is Contraindicated or cannot be performed

criteria.description: Patient has new progressive neurological deficit localizing to the thoracic spine (e.g., extremity weakness, bowel/bladder dysfunction, gait instability)
Thoracic spine MRI is contraindicated (e.g. non-MRI-compatible device, severe claustrophobia) or cannot be performed

required_documentation: Clinical notes detailing progressive thoracic neurological deficits and explicit contraindication to MRI
rules.review_notes: Thoracic CT for neurologic deficits when MRI is contraindicated.

rules.source_section: INDICATIONS FOR THORACIC SPINE CT / Evaluation of Back Pain (1) / Pain lasting > 4 weeks

criteria.description: Persistent thoracic back pain lasting greater than 4 weeks
Failure of at least 4-6 weeks of conservative management including physical therapy or medications
Thoracic spine MRI is contraindicated or cannot be performed

required_documentation: Progress notes documenting pain duration, conservative treatment dates and modalities, and MRI contraindication
rules.review_notes: Thoracic CT for chronic thoracic pain after failed conservative therapy when MRI contraindicated.
